description: Committee recommends approving payroll audit terms of reference.
Audit assesses city's payroll process controls.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Moves public notice for external borrowing closer to project start.
Eliminates public notice for internal capital project borrowing.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Committee recommends acquiring 1.9 square metres for a 3rd Avenue North sidewalk.
The land from Frie Investments Ltd. would cost $2,500.

chips.text: Recommended
Frie Investments Ltd. as land seller

description: City to sell 2011 1st Avenue North property for $1.28 million.
Proceeds will fund future city property purchases.
Property no longer needed for fire department.

chips.text: Recommended
Proceeds from sale will go into the city's Property Realized Reserve.

description: Recommends $1 million for Brighton bus rapid transit extension.
Funds transferred from Housing Accelerator Fund to meet housing targets.

chips.text: Recommended
$200k unallocated, $400k housing Saskatoon, $250k Brownfield, $150k affordable housing.
Councillor thanked administration for a "creative solution" to future budget pressure.
Residents of Brighton neighborhood will get extended bus rapid transit service.
$150,000 for affordable housing site remediation is reallocated from the fund.
Extension of red line to Brighton accelerated due to new high schools.

description: Recommend a below-market lease for a drop-in centre at 130 Idylwyld.
Recommend a new reserve for building operations and maintenance.
Recommend a tax exemption for 130 Idylwyld Drive North up to 5 years.

chips.text: Recommended
Tax exemption would forgo $18,000 city tax and $1,800 library tax annually.
Saskatoon Tribal Council will operate the drop-in centre.
Residents are uncomfortable with the city's financial contributions.
Councilor Deball opposed due to concerns about the city's financial burden.
Staff will provide a future report on annual homelessness response costs.

description: City explored proposal to increase affordable housing fund to 25%.
Other civic projects would receive less funding as a result.

chips.text: Proposed increasing affordable housing allocation from 15% to 25%.
Taxpayers could face higher property taxes for civic projects.
Increased funding would strengthen city's affordable housing contributions.

description: City capital projects are $32 million under budget.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois highlighted projects are not over budget, contrary to public rhetoric.
